record.context_brief: Large sum-free subsets of integer sets
record.original_question: What is the largest constant c with the property that any nite, su ciently large set A of integers contains a sum-free subset of size at least cjAj? Recall, that a subset A of an additively written group is called sum-free, if A \ (A + A) = ?; that is, the equation x + y = z has no solutions in the elements of A. (Thus, Schur's theorem, discussed in the Introduction, says that the set of positive integers cannot be partitioned into nitely many sum-free subsets.) Alon and Kleitman showed in , as a slight improvement of a result of Erd}os from , that any nite set A of non-zero integers contains a sum-free subset with at least l jAj+1 m elements. Bourgain , using an elaborate Fourier analysis technique, improved this further to l jAj+2 m . There is no indication that the factor 1=3 is best possible here, though it is shown in that it cannot be replaced by a number, larger than 12=29. 3. artifact.self_contained_problem:
A subset B of an additively written abelian group is called sum-free if there are no solutions to the equation x + y = z with x, y, z ∈ B (equivalently, B ∩ (B + B) = ∅). For a finite set A of integers, let s(A) denote the size of the largest sum-free subset of A. Define

  c = sup { c' ≥ 0 : for every sufficiently large finite set A ⊂ ℤ, s(A) ≥ c' · |A| }.

Determine the exact value of c. (Known classical bounds give c ≥ 1/3, while constructions show c ≤ 12/29.)
artifact.status_search_result: Eberhard, Green, and Manners (2014) proved that for every ε > 0 there exists a finite set A of integers in which every subset of size at least (1/3 + ε)|A| contains a solution to x + y = z, establishing that the optimal constant is c = 1/3. Bedert (2025) further showed the lower bound can be strengthened to N/3 + (log log N)-type additive growth, but the linear constant 1/3 is provably optimal. The original question of identifying the constant c is therefore resolved (c = 1/3); the precise asymptotic of the lower-order term remains open.

status_evidence.title: Sets of integers with no large sum-free subset (Eberhard–Green–Manners)
status_evidence.snippet: For every ε>0 there is a set A of n integers such that every subset of size at least (1/3+ε)n contains x,y,z with x+y=z.
status_evidence.claim: The constant 1/3 in Erdős' theorem is optimal.

status_evidence.title: Graduate Student Solves Classic Problem About the Limits of Addition
status_evidence.snippet: Bedert proved any set of N integers has a sum-free subset with at least N/3 + log(log N) elements.
status_evidence.claim: Bedert improved the additive lower-order term while the linear constant 1/3 stays optimal.
